MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Drive growth. Build trusted clinical partnerships. Shape the future of private healthcare.

St Vincent's Private Hospital Toowoomba is seeking an accomplished Business Development Manager to lead specialist engagement, doctor recruitment and strategic growth initiatives across one of Queensland's most respected private hospitals.

This is an outstanding opportunity for a seasoned relationship-builder who thrives in complex stakeholder environments and can confidently engage with specialists, practice managers, GPs and senior health leaders.

Reporting to the State Business Development Manager and working closely with the General Manager, you will play a critical role in growth key specialty services, strengthening referral pathways and supporting the recruitment and retention of Visiting Medical Officers (VMOs).

If you're commercially astute, highly credible and passionate about building long-term partnerships that deliver sustainable growth, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

As Business Development Manager, you will:

Drive specialty growth strategies aligned to the hospital's strategic priorities

Develop and maintain trusted relationships with specialist doctors, VMOs, practice managers and referring GPs

Identify, recruit and onboard new specialists to support service growth.

Analyse market opportunities, referral patterns and business performance data to identity growth opportunities

Contribute to the development of business cases and strategic growth initiatives that deliver measurable outcomes

Lead doctor engagement activities, education events, and referral development programs

Partner with hospital leadership and marketing teams to execute business development and marketing strategies

Maintain a strong pipeline of opportunities through CRM and business intelligence reporting

About you:

You are an experienced commercial professional with a proven ability to build credibility in specialist healthcare environments.

You will ideally bring:

Significant experience in healthcare business development, clinical network development, healthcare sales or hospital engagement.

A demonstrated track record of influencing and building relationships with specialists, surgeons, physicians and referrers.

Strong communication acumen with experience developing business cases and growth strategies.

Exceptional stakeholder management, presentation and negotiation skills.

Experience working autonomously while partnering effectively with executive leaders.

A strategic mindset combined with a hands-on approach to execution.

Experience within private hospitals, healthcare services or specialist healthcare networks will be highly regarded.

Qualifications in Business, Commerce, Health or a related discipline are desirable.

Why join St Vincent's Health Australia?

Make a genuine impact within Australia's largest for purpose health and aged care provider.

Work alongside highly respected clinical and executive leaders.

Competitive salary and salary packaging benefits.

Up to $15,990 salary packaging plus Meals and Entertainment benefits.

Private health insurance discounts through Medibank and Bupa.

Additional leave purchase options.

Access to Fitness Passport and Employee Assistance Program.

Blue Light Card discounts across hundreds of retailers.

About St Vincent's Private Hospital Toowoomba

St Vincent's Private Hospital Toowoomba is the largest acute private hospital on the Darling Downs, delivering exceptional care across more than 30 specialties including surgical, cardiac, cancer, maternity, emergency and medical services. 

As part of St Vincent's Health Australia, we are driven by our values of Compassion, Excellence, Integrity and Justice, and are committed to delivering outstanding patient-centred care to our community. 

Mission and Values:

As both a provider of care and as an employer, St Vincent's aspires to create an environment that is truly inclusive for all people, always. St Vincent's is constantly striving for inclusivity and to create and cherish a diverse place of care and work.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.

Creating and updating appropriate documentation relating to the SCV ASM application.












Supporting and troubleshooting for application issues.












Liaising with Monash Health employees to address simple 'how to' questions.












Develop maintenance schedule.












Co-ordinate and-or facilitate upgrades ensuring testing and user notification.












Liaise with vendor regarding issues.












Publish training and manual for resources for user community.












Create and manage users' accounts and security rights.












Ensuring Central tickets are managed in a timely manner and closed off with appropriate levels of documentation.












Professional and customer focused communications via both the Central ticket management system and phone.












Maintain and adhere to operational procedures and complete appropriate support documentation when procedures change.












Develop and maintain a customer focused culture and contribute to a friendly and co-operative working environment, fostering strong working relationships with all colleagues to deliver quality outcomes.












Build and leverage relationships internally with Digital and Information Division teams such as Service Desk, Infrastructure, Desktop Experience, and Support Services.












Participate in ad hoc projects as directed by Director of Application Services.












Other duties as assigned from time to time by the Head of Partner Applications.









About You






Qualifications, registrations and licences:









Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or a related field preferred.












Prior experience in a system administrator role or similar.










Technical skills, knowledge and experience: 









Excellent verbal-written communication and documentation skills.












A strong desire and capability to listen, analyse and recommend.












Excellent interpersonal and relationship building skills.












Excellent time and personnel management skills.












Ability to work within deadlines.












Ability to work unsupervised.












Experience with clinical communication systems or healthcare IT. 






Good knowledge of Microsoft 365 platform and Teams functionality








For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Liz Feeny - Head of Partner Applications on 0412 032 226.



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'

Having excellent communication skills

Exceptional attention to detail

A strong customer service focus

Make a meaningful difference with BlueCare

Child safe, Child friendly

Diversity & Inclusion

In this rewarding role, you will take responsibility for the organisation and day-to-day operation of your designated pharmacy area, driving best-practice pharmacy services in line with professional standards, hospital policies and quality use of medicines principles. You will collaborate with pharmacists, technicians, assistants, interns and students, providing guidance and support while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and clinical excellence. Exceptional Communication and Teamwork Skills - Possess highly developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build strong relationships and work collaboratively with medical, nursing and allied health professionals.

Analytical, Organised and Results-Focused - Demonstrate strong problem-solving, research and data analysis capabilities, coupled with excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to supervise, mentor and develop staff in a fast-paced healthcare setting.

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need.

Full-time Wall and Floor Tiler position available with a competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Hurlstone Park, NSW 2193

•	Full-Time Position
•	$80,000 - $90,000 plus superannuation 
•	Operate within a professional setting.

FerMax Stone Pty Ltd is an Australian company established in 2012, specialising in the installation of premium wall and floor tiling, natural stone, porcelain and other high-quality surface finishes for residential and commercial projects. Since its establishment, the company has built a reputation for delivering quality workmanship, reliability and exceptional customer service across a wide range of projects.
On behalf of our client, we are looking for an experienced and skilled Wall and Floor tiler to join our team on a full-time basis

Position Responsibilities and Tasks

As a Wall and Floor Tiler, your duties will include, but will not be limited to:

•	Interpret plans and specifications; confirm measurements, quantities, layout lines and levels prior to commencing tiling works.
•	Measure, mark and set out surfaces using levelling equipment (including laser levels) to establish correct alignment, falls and datum lines.
•	Measure, cut, shape and install custom heritage mosaic tiles and decorative stone finishes, ensuring accurate pattern alignment, preserving heritage design features and delivering high-quality workmanship in accordance with project specifications.
•	Prepare wall and floor substrates by removing old tiles, grout and adhesives; filling holes and cracks; and cleaning/priming surfaces to ensure suitable adhesion and finish.
•	Lay and fix tiles (including ceramic, clay, slate, marble, glass and similar materials) to internal and external walls and floors to achieve required patterns, alignment and tolerances.
•	Apply adhesives and bedding materials to substrates and/or tile backs as required, ensuring correct coverage, bonding and curing in line with product specifications.
•	Cut, shape and fit tiles using hand and power tile-cutting tools to finish edges, corners and penetrations around fittings, pipes and fixtures.
•	Maintain consistent alignment and spacing throughout installation, checking for lippage, level, line and falls, and adjusting as required during installation.
•	Complete grouting, finishing and clean-down, including removing excess grout and presenting a consistent, defect-free surface finish.
•	Support waterproofing outcomes by assisting with waterproofing preparation/detailing and coordinating tiling works with waterproofing stages and inspection hold points, ensuring correct detailing at junctions and penetrations in wet areas and external areas.
•	Undertake substrate preparation activities that support tiling quality (e.g., grinding, levelling and surface preparation), and coordinate transitions/interfaces with epoxy or other protective floor finishes where required by project scope.
•	Work collaboratively on major construction sites across Sydney/NSW, liaising with site foremen and project managers regarding sequencing, access, quality inspections and program timeframes.
•	Maintain compliance with WHS requirements, including safe manual handling, correct PPE use, silica dust controls and safe operation of plant and tools used for cutting and surface preparation.


Qualifications and Skills:

•	Certificate III in Wall and Floor Tiling or relevant trade qualification.
•	At least two years of relevant experience.
•	Sound knowledge of wall and floor tiling techniques and installation methods.
•	Experience working with ceramic, porcelain, marble, granite and natural stone products.
•	Ability to read and interpret plans and technical drawings.
•	Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality workmanship.

Salary:
The role offers a remuneration package of $80,000 - $90,000 per annum, plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

The Dermatology Research position at Royal North Shore Hospital (RNSH) offers a unique opportunity for junior doctors and research-focused clinicians to develop expertise in clinical research while working alongside leading dermatologists and academic researchers.

Based within a major tertiary referral hospital, this role provides exposure to a broad range of dermatological conditions, including inflammatory skin disease, skin cancer, complex medical dermatology and emerging therapeutic treatments. The successful applicant will contribute to a variety of research activities, including clinical studies, data collection and analysis, literature reviews, ethics submissions, manuscript preparation and presentation of findings at scientific meetings.

Working within a collaborative multidisciplinary environment, the position supports the development of skills in research methodology, critical appraisal, project management and academic writing. Participants may also have opportunities to engage with clinical dermatology services, attend educational meetings and contribute to quality improvement initiatives.

Royal North Shore Hospital has a strong reputation for excellence in research, education and clinical care, with close links to academic institutions and research organisations across Northern Sydney. The role provides an excellent platform for doctors interested in Dermatology, Academic Medicine, Physician Training or future clinician-researcher careers.

This position is ideal for highly motivated individuals seeking to strengthen their research portfolio while contributing to projects that improve patient outcomes and advance knowledge in dermatological medicine.

Where you'll be working - Royal North Shore Hospital

Royal North Shore Hospital (RNSH) is a principal tertiary referral hospital within Northern Sydney Local Health District, delivering a comprehensive range of complex and highly specialised healthcare services to patients across Northern Sydney and New South Wales.

Renowned for its excellence in clinical care, education and research, RNSH has a long and proud history of providing world-class healthcare while supporting the training and development of future healthcare professionals. The hospital offers a broad range of specialist services, including major trauma, severe burns, spinal cord injury management, neonatal intensive care, bone marrow transplantation, neurosurgery and interventional neuroradiology. These services are complemented by comprehensive acute medical, surgical, mental health, paediatric, cancer and maternity care programs.

The RNSH campus is also home to The Kolling, a leading medical research institute jointly governed by Northern Sydney Local Health District and the University of Sydney, fostering innovation and translational research that improves patient outcomes and advances healthcare delivery.

Working at RNSH provides the opportunity to be part of a leading health service committed to clinical excellence, innovation, education and research, while making a meaningful difference to the lives of patients and their families.

This is an excellent opportunity for a reliable and detail-oriented professional to become an integral member of De Walkers Group and contribute to the cost planning, procurement and successful delivery of our residential construction projects.      Responsibilities   As a Quantity Surveyor, your primary responsibilities will include:   Obtaining quotations from subcontractors, suppliers and vendors, collating and assessing the quotations received, and providing recommendations to management.  Reviewing architectural drawings, engineering plans, project specifications and contract documentation to determine the labour, materials, equipment and other resources required for each project.  Preparing detailed construction cost estimates based on project drawings, specifications and supporting contract documentation.  Undertaking accurate quantity take-offs using modern estimating technologies and recognised methods of measurement.  Preparing bills of quantities, schedules of rates, tender documentation and other project costing documents. Preparing rate analyses and cost comparisons to assist management with tender evaluation and procurement decisions.  Assisting with the preparation and evaluation of tenders, subcontractor packages and supplier procurement documentation.  Monitoring project expenditure throughout all stages of construction to ensure that projects remain aligned with the approved baseline cost plan and budget.  Identifying cost deviations, potential overruns and financial risks and recommending appropriate corrective measures.  Preparing regular project cost reports, cash-flow forecasts, cost-to-complete assessments and financial updates for management.  Identifying and establishing the scope of proposed changes to construction works.  Evaluating and pricing client change requests, contract variations and extension of time claims. We are seeking applications from Senior Occupational Therapists to join our OT Rehab at Home service, on a casual roster with potential permanent positions available in the next 3 to 6 months. As a Senior Occupational Therapist - Grade 2 or 3 depending on your experience, you'll join a collaborative multidisciplinary team, delivering high-quality, client-centred occupational therapy services that empower people to achieve their goals and maintain independence in the comfort of their own homes.

This senior role offers the opportunity to apply your specialist clinical expertise, work independently, and influence best practice across the service. You'll also play a key role in mentoring and developing junior clinicians, supervising students, and contributing to education, quality improvement, and research initiatives that shape the future of care.

At St John of God Healthcare at Home, we're transforming the way healthcare is delivered. Our home visiting service enables people to recover from surgery or manage ongoing health needs in the familiar surroundings of their own home. By partnering with clients and their families, we provide personalised, flexible care that helps people feel safe, confident, and in control throughout their healthcare journey. From hospital-in-the-home programs to ongoing community-based support, you'll have the opportunity to deliver care where it matters most, making a lasting difference in the lives of those you support.

We are the At-Home Team for each of the SJOG hospitals across WA and work out of the Osborn Park Office, SJG Murdoch and SJG Midland hospitals to accommodate most metro areas.

This position will be offered on a casual basis with an expectation of 1-2 shifts weekly depending on caseload with potential permanent positions available in the next 3 to 6 months.

In conjunction with the Supervisor-Manager and other Occupational Therapy caregivers, develop processes for the evaluation of both inpatient and outpatient Occupational Therapy programs.

Put patients-clients plans in place and monitor outcomes regularly through attendance at and participation in multi-disciplinary team meetings.

Strive for high satisfaction levels of patients, clients and external agencies.

Complete appropriate administrative duties. Liaise with the administration team, report statistical data and ensure completion of progress notes.

Act as a clinical consultant for the discipline and within the specialty.

Exercise independent professional judgment on routine matters. Obtain direct professional supervision from more senior caregivers when performing novel, complex or critical tasks.

We are looking for those who enjoy working collaboratively, are committed to continuous improvement and keen to contribute to innovative clinical practice while supporting the development of others. To succeed in this role, you will hold a Tertiary qualification in Occupational Therapy and current registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA). You'll bring senior clinical experience, ideally within healthcare or disability services, along with a passion for delivering evidence-based, persocentred care. Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

Objective
To be a key member of the Mission to Seafarers South Australia team, providing welfare services to visiting seafarers while supporting the sustainable development and operation of Mission to Seafarers centres across South Australia.
Based in Port Pirie, the Port Welfare Officers will share responsibility for providing seafarer welfare services, supporting volunteers and committees, coordinating administration, and assisting with the development of services in all South Australian ports, including Port Adelaide,  Port Lincoln, Port Giles, Thevenard, Wallaroo and any future centres established within the state.
The role combines practical seafarer welfare, volunteer coordination, administration, stakeholder engagement and centre development.

Level of Responsibility
The Port Welfare Officers report directly to the Regional Director, Mission to Seafarers Australia.
They work closely with the South Australian Management Committee, local port committees, volunteers, port authorities, shipping agents, churches and other stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of welfare services throughout the state.

The role shares responsibility for:
Day-to-day operation of the Port Pirie Seafarers Centre.
Development and support of Mission to Seafarers activities throughout South Australia.
Volunteer recruitment, training and support.
Administrative and financial management of the South Australian operations.
Regular travel to South Australian ports to visit ships, support volunteers and strengthen relationships with industry partners.

Conditions
The successful applicant will be required to maintain:
Current Driver's Licence.
National Police Check.
Safe Church Communities accreditation (or equivalent).
Working With Children Check (or applicable state screening requirements).
Australian Border Force and Port Security access requirements as required.
Capacity to travel throughout South Australia, including overnight travel where necessary.

About the Role
This position would suit someone who is passionate about improving the welfare of seafarers, enjoys working with volunteers and industry, is highly organised, flexible and self-motivated, and is comfortable working across multiple locations.
The role requires initiative, strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with maritime industry stakeholders while developing sustainable welfare services across regional ports.

Knowledge and Experience
The successful applicant will possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills together with confidence using technology.
A sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Xero or similar accounting software, databases, social media and web-based systems is desirable.

Essential Skills and Experience
Office administration experience.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Experience using accounting software (preferably Xero).
Experience coordinating volunteers or community programs.
Current driver's licence and willingness to travel.
Desirable Skills and Experience
Experience preparing agendas, minutes and financial reports.
Website and social media management.
Marketing and communications experience.
Fundraising and grant administration.
Community development experience.
Understanding of the Mission to Seafarers and the maritime industry.
Experience working with committees or not-for-profit organisations.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. Seafarer Welfare
Visit ships and provide welfare support to visiting seafarers.
Coordinate transport, shopping, communications and welfare services.
Supply SIM cards, Wi-Fi access and welfare items.
Assist with emergency welfare situations when required.
Promote compliance with the Maritime Labour Convention welfare provisions.
2. Centre and Port Development
Support the ongoing development of Mission to Seafarers services throughout South Australia.
Assist with establishing and growing welfare activities in new and developing ports.
Identify opportunities to improve facilities and services.
Build relationships with port authorities, shipping agents, terminal operators and industry stakeholders.
Promote awareness of seafarer welfare across the maritime community.
3. Administration
Prepare agendas, reports and committee meeting minutes.
Complete and maintain Australian Border Force documentation.
Maintain registrations, licences and compliance records.
Monitor donations and acknowledge supporters.
Support committee office bearers with administration.
Manage SIM cards, vouchers and foreign currency.
Assist the Regional Director with reporting and projects.
4. Communications and Marketing
Monitor incoming enquiries.
Coordinate communications with volunteers, shipping agents and port stakeholders.
Maintain websites and social media platforms.
Produce promotional material highlighting Mission activities.
Represent Mission to Seafarers at community and industry events.
5. Volunteer Management
Recruit new volunteers across South Australia.
Coordinate induction, training and mentoring.
Maintain volunteer records and compliance.
Coordinate Working With Children Checks, port inductions, First Aid and other required training.
Develop volunteer rosters where applicable.
6. Financial Administration
Assist with day-to-day financial administration.
Process invoices and expenses.
Support budgeting and financial reporting.
Maintain accurate records using Xero or equivalent systems.
7. Stakeholder Engagement
Develop productive relationships with:
Flinders Ports
Shipping agents
Maritime unions
AMSA
Australian Border Force
Port Welfare Committees
Local churches
Community organisations
Government agencies
Represent Mission to Seafarers at meetings and forums as required.
8. Attendance
Attend:
South Australian committee meetings.
National Mission to Seafarers conferences.
Volunteer training events.
Industry meetings and conferences.
Ship visits across South Australian ports.
Other duties as directed by the Regional Director.

Employment Conditions
The position is offered as a job-share arrangement, with two Port Welfare Officers working collaboratively to provide consistent coverage across South Australia.
The combined role is funded at 5Days per week, with flexibility to increase hours through project funding or centre development initiatives.
Regular travel throughout South Australia is an essential component of the role, with a Mission vehicle available where appropriate.
Comprehensive on-the-job training will be provided.
The role would suit someone with several years of workplace experience who enjoys working with people, is comfortable travelling, and wants to make a meaningful contribution to the wellbeing of international seafarers visiting South Australian ports.

Make a meaningful difference with The Wesley Private Hospital 

The Wesley Hospital is one of Australia's iconic and largest private not-for-profit hospitals. From the heart of Brisbane, more than 800 Visiting Medical Practitioners and 2,000 staff deliver personalised care through life's journey making a meaningful difference in the lives of generations of Queenslanders. We offer comprehensive care across a wide range of acute tertiary-level medical and surgical services with a particular focus on cancer care, cardiac care, women's and children's care, and complex surgical care. This includes the busiest robotic surgery program and the first Robotic Surgery Centre of Excellence accredited in Australia. 

An integral part of our team, as a Security Officer, you'll be encouraged to grow, develop and feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. Let's make a meaningful difference, together!

What you will be doing
Two positions are offered, working within the Haematology Clinical Research Unit and Department of Haematology at Concord Hospital. The positions are open to qualified candidates in Clinical Haematology. Opportunities are available to develop your own research projects including enrolment in a higher research degree if desired. Fellows are encouraged to develop an area of research interest and to present at local, state and national meetings where appropriate. 

1.Clinical Research Unit (CRU) Fellow

a.The CRU Fellow manages patients treated in clinical trials across all haematological malignancies. They will gain valuable experience in managing patients treated with bispecific-trispecific antibodies and novel small molecules in phase I, II and III trials. They will work closely with the CAR T fellow in care of patients in CAR T trials.

b.They will provide both routine and urgent medical assessment and clinical care to patients screened & participating in clinical trials as a certified Investigator within Concord Haematology's Clinical Research Unit (CRU).

c.They will also be involved in supporting observational studies and disease registries.

2.Haemostasis & Thrombosis (H&T) Fellow

a.Management of patients on H&T clinical trials

b.Co-ordination of participants involved in H&T translational and observational research projects and registries. Potential for engagement with translational projects in collaboration with the ANZAC research institute.

c.Participation in specialty clinics: Inherited Platelet Disorders Clinic, clinics with Antiphospholipid Syndrome focus and general H&T clinics

d.Providing H&T consultative services within the hospital, including ICU H&T rounds, and coagulation laboratory support

e.Co-leading H&T governance activities including: VTE Prevention-Anticoagulation Stewardship meetings, Concord and District anticoagulation guideline updates

f.Providing rapid access outpatient service for management of acute VTE

The Concord Haematology Clinical Research Unit (HCRU)
Concord HCRU is a large and growing clinical research unit which supports Concord Haematology department goal to deliver "world class care locally". Housed in the purpose built Concord Cancer Centre, we undertake early to late phase clinical trials including CAR-T clinical trials and first-in-human phase I trials. The trials portfolio extends across a broad range of malignancies (lymphoma, leukaemia, myeloma, MDS) and other haematological disorders (thrombosis, autoimmune disorders). At any one time, the HCRU manages more than 120 studies either recruiting or in follow up from phase I-IV.

Under the leadership of the HCRU Haematologist Director and Manager, the HCRU supports 9 clinical haematologists and employs 13 clinical research nurses - study coordinators, 4 administrative staff responsible for ethics and regulatory requirements as well as 4 medical student data managers, and patient investigators. The Unit has a strong ethos of community engagement and its investigator-initiated research is supported by the Foundation for A Bloody Great Cause!

Where you will be working

Concord Repatriation General Hospital (CRGH) is a principal referral facility and a teaching hospital of the University of Sydney in the geographical centre of Sydney. CRGH offers a comprehensive range of specialty and sub-specialty services, many recognised nationally and internationally as Centre's of excellence. The affiliated ANZAC Research Institute performs high quality basic and translational research, in particular, the Platelet and Thrombosis Research Group led by Prof Vivien Chen.

Concord Haematology offers full clinical and laboratory services including autologous stem cell transplantation and apheresis unit, a large treatment and outpatient service as well as a general consultation service. Haematologists within the unit have strong ties to Working Groups in the Australasian Leukaemia and Lymphoma Group, representation on the Australasian Lymphoma Alliance and have many active national and international collaborations.

With your skills and experience, you can contribute to the millions of ways we're enriching health, and develop your career as part of the largest health organisation in Australia. 
 

Achieve Something Great 
Join the South Western Sydney Local Health District (SWSLHD) Public Health Unit and contribute to protecting and improving the health of one of Australia's largest and most culturally diverse communities. As a Registered Nurse within the Communicable Diseases Team, you will play a key role in the assessment, management, and prevention of notifiable communicable diseases, working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders to deliver consistent, high-quality public health services. 

Based in Liverpool CBD, you will be part of a multidisciplinary Public Health Unit that includes Communicable Diseases, Immunisation, Environmental Health, and Administration teams, alongside Doctors, Nurses, Epidemiologists, and Data Quality Administrators dedicated to improving community health outcomes.

Are You the Right Fit? 
We are seeking a passionate nurse with a strong interest in public health and communicable disease management who thrives in a multidisciplinary team environment. You will possess exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to use telephone and other communication platforms to gather and convey critical information for the assessment and management of communicable diseases in an engaging, sensitive, and culturally appropriate manner. You will provide advice and support to healthcare professionals, aged care facilities, disability providers, schools, childcare centres, and other community stakeholders, helping to protect people and communities at risk of infection. 

If you are collaborative, adaptable, and committed to improving public health across South Western Sydney, this rewarding role offers the opportunity to make a genuine difference, including participation in after-hours and weekend coverage with medical support.

Cox Purtell  
  Senior Salesforce System Administrator  
 You know Salesforce is only as strong as the way it is looked after. 
 Clean access. Sensible configuration. Stable releases. Good support. Strong governance. A platform people can actually rely on. 
 That is what this role is about. 
 You'll be joining a Brisbane-based university using Salesforce across existing and new platforms, including CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud. Some of the environment is established. Some of it is being improved and remediated. Your role will be to help look after the whole platform, not just one narrow part of it. 
 This will suit you if you are a hands-on Salesforce Administrator who likes ownership, cares about platform quality, and enjoys being close to the people who use the system. 
  The role  
 As the Senior Salesforce System Administrator, you'll help keep Salesforce stable, secure and useful across a large university environment. 
 You'll work across day-to-day administration, user support, configuration, platform improvement, release support and governance. 
 You'll be the person helping make sure Salesforce is well managed across CRM, marketing, engagement, alumni-style use cases and Education Cloud. 
 You'll work with the Salesforce Program Manager, architects, business analysts, DevOps specialists and business stakeholders. You won't be working in isolation, but you will be trusted to take real ownership of the admin layer of the platform. 
  What you'll be doing  
 You'll manage Salesforce users, roles, profiles, permission sets, licences and access controls. 
 You'll support Salesforce CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud usage across existing and new platform areas. 
 You'll provide practical support to users, helping resolve issues and improve how teams use Salesforce. 
 You'll configure Salesforce using declarative tools such as Flow, Approval Processes, Assignment Rules, Lightning pages, page layouts and permission structures. 
 You'll support sandbox management, release management and controlled deployment processes. 
 You'll help identify technical debt, platform risks, security issues and improvement opportunities. 
 You'll document changes, support adoption and create guidance that helps users get better value from Salesforce. 
 You'll help improve and remediate the platform while also keeping the current environment running properly. 
  What we're looking for  
 You'll bring strong hands-on Salesforce administration experience. 
 You might currently be a Salesforce Administrator, Senior Salesforce Administrator, Salesforce System Administrator, Salesforce Platform Administrator or Salesforce Consultant with strong admin capability. 
 Higher education experience would be useful, but it is not essential. 
 Experience in adjacent environments would be very relevant, particularly CRM, marketing, membership, alumni, engagement, customer service or stakeholder management platforms. 
 You'll be comfortable working in a complex Salesforce environment where different teams use the platform in different ways. 
 You'll understand Salesforce security, user access, profiles, permission sets, configuration, support and release processes. 
 Salesforce Administrator certification is preferred. If you are not certified yet but are actively working towards it, we are still happy to talk. 
  Why this role could be interesting  
 You'll have genuine ownership of a high-impact Salesforce platform. 
 You'll be involved in both improvement and remediation, not just routine ticket work. 
 You'll work across broad Salesforce use cases, including CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud. 
 You'll be part of a major university environment where Salesforce supports real engagement with students, staff, partners and alumni. 
 You'll have the chance to help create a strong higher-ed Salesforce case study. 
  Location  
 The university is based in Brisbane. 
 Brisbane-based candidates are very welcome and would spend regular time in the office. 
 We can also consider candidates in Sydney, Melbourne or other eastern Australian cities, provided you are willing to travel to Brisbane occasionally. As a guide, there will be an expectation to attend the Brisbane office at least once per month. 
  Work rights  
 We can only consider candidates with full work rights in Australia. 
 You will need to be an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or New Zealand citizen. 
  Key details  
 Role: Senior Salesforce System Administrator Platform: Salesforce CRM, Marketing and Education Cloud Contract: 12-month fixed term contract, likely to extend Package: $160,000 plus superannuation Location: Brisbane preferred; Sydney, Melbourne and other eastern Australian cities considered Work rights: Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or New Zealand citizen only 
  Interested?  
 Apply with your CV or get in touch for a confidential conversation. 
 This is a strong role if you want to own, improve and support a Salesforce platform that matters.

About the Opportunity  

 A bulk billing medical centre in the industrial inner city suburbs of Beaconsfield is needing at least 3 x vocationally registered general practitioners to join their dedicated team of medical and healthcare professionals in supporting growth of the practice and increasing patient demand from new and existing patients. Located in the spot of a medical clinic that operated in the same location for 10 years next to a pharmacy, supermarkets, diagnostic imaging their patient base consists of a healthy mix of educated, easygoing young families, retirees and young working professionals who need pre-employment medicals or work cover appointments. In addition to new patients from the local community this purpose-built medical centre has taken over a database of 20,000 patients from a nearby medical centre less than 4km away hence the urgent need for more doctors to help distribute their patient load. Shifts are flexible and no weekend work is required. You will be working in a well-known location with great coffee, high end technology, spacious consultation rooms, nursing/administration/management support with above average billings for chronic disease management so  APPLY  now with your latest CV and don’t miss out on a great opportunity! 

  Essential Criteria:  

 
	 MBBS or equivalent 
	 Must have a current and valid AHPRA GENERAL /SPECIALIST registration 
	 FRACGP qualified 
	 Team Player 
   Apply Now
